The DATA 471 notes built [convolutional layers](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-convolutional-layer) by hand,
with [padding](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-padding),
[stride](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-stride),
[pooling](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-pooling)
and [channels](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-channel).
This lecture puts them to work in PyTorch:

1.  the [shape](pytorch-basics.qmd#def-shape)s that `nn.Conv2d` takes and returns;
2.  how far across the image one output of a stack of layers can see;
3.  what happens to a convolutional network, and to an [MLP](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-feedforward-network), when a digit moves by one pixel;
4.  a short history of the architectures built from these layers;
5.  reusing a network trained on one task to start another.
